note: The headline number did not move and is not claimed to. `distinct` went 60% -> 100% on the DISTINCT repair (#58), a mechanical +6 attempts; `date`, `group_by` and `having` gave back 9 between them, and every case behind those losses is already listed under non_deterministic or was failing before. 87.1 sits inside the band the previous baseline recorded, so this is one sample of a noisy measurement — not a regression and not an improvement. Only the per-category distinct figure is a real change.

previous.note: After the GROUP BY key repair (#52), before the DISTINCT repair (#58).

known_failures.note: #58 is fixed deterministically and `distinct` is now 15/15. #59 and #60 remain open: prompt fixes for both were written, measured and reverted — see PROJECT_STATUS.md. What remains is dominated by date handling, which is now the largest single category loss and has no issue of its own yet.

always_failing.sales_cheapest_product: #59 — returns the measure, not the entity: SELECT MIN(price) instead of the product
always_failing.emp_joined_2021: a year-range filter becomes an equality test against a single date (join_date = '2021-01-01')
always_failing.emp_joined_before_2020: projects an extra column the reference does not (emp_name, join_date vs emp_name)

floor_rationale: 80 sits 6 points below the lowest observed round (86.0) and is unchanged. The floor detects a regression, not a target: it trips if a whole category collapses, but not on this model's ordinary run-to-run variance — of which this round is a good illustration. Raise it only when a real improvement lands and the *category* figures, not the headline, show it.
